3. Present petition is filed under Section 528 B.N.S.S. to quash the entire proceedings of Sessions Trial No. 54 of 2025 'State Vs. Vipin Saxena' under Sections 376 and 506 I.P.C. pending in the court of learned Sessions Court, Udham Singh Nagar.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner/accused would submit that an F.I.R. was lodged by the respondent no.2/complainant against the petitioner alleging therein that the petitioner/accused had established physical relations with the respondent no.2/complainant on false pretext of marriage.

He would further submit that the petitioner is innocent person and has falsely been implicated in the present case; that, the respondent no.2/complainant is already married woman and she has two children from that marriage; that, the physical relationship between the petitioner and the respondent no.2/complainant was purely consensual in nature.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that as per a recent judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amol Bhagwan Nehul vs. State of Maharashtra, (2025) SCC OnLine SC 1230, it has been held that no offence under Section 376 I.P.C. is made out where the prosecutrix was married at the time of the alleged incident.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner/accused would submit that an F.I.R. was lodged by the respondent no.2/complainant against the petitioner alleging therein that the petitioner/accused had established physical relations with the respondent no.2/complainant on false pretext of marriage.
He would further submit that the petitioner is innocent person and has falsely been implicated in the present case; that, the respondent no.2/complainant is already married woman and she has two children from that marriage; that, the physical relationship between the petitioner and the respondent no.2/complainant was purely consensual in nature.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that as per a recent judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amol Bhagwan Nehul vs. State of Maharashtra, (2025) SCC OnLine SC 1230, it has been held that no offence under Section 376 I.P.C. is made out where the prosecutrix was married at the time of the alleged incident.
He would further submit that the FIR in question was lodged by respondent no.2/complainant only to exert undue pressure upon the petitioner/accused and to settle personal scores or grievances,
therefore, the entire criminal proceeding is unsustainable in the eyes of law and is liable to be quashed.
5. Per contra, learned State counsel would submit that serious allegations have been levelled against the petitioner.
